body.x: The Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that it opened the “Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion” at CES 2026, which opened on January 6 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States, and that it is presenting Incheon’s urban strategy to visitors from around the world.

The Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion spans 139 square meters in the AI Zone of the North Hall at the Las Vegas Convention Center. The pavilion puts Incheon’s “AI City” vision at the forefront and introduces the city’s innovation direction on the global stage.

Under the theme “Destination Incheon — From Smart City to AI City,” the pavilion features three themed zones that systematically showcase AI-based urban services and innovation models applied across daily life, industry, and culture, and present a vision for a sustainable future city. The zones highlight residential environments that enhance citizen services such as mobility, safety, energy, and health; workplaces that drive innovation across industrial sectors, including manufacturing, logistics, food, and pharmaceuticals; and creative urban spaces that generate content and experiences.

Key programs included the Global AI City Forum, which brought together global urban and industry experts to share Incheon’s next-generation AI city strategy and directions for cooperation. In particular, an exchange session with Fairfax County was built on the economic development cooperation between the two sides and discussed ways to expand collaboration in areas such as innovation ecosystem development, startup support, and technology demonstration.

body.cap: Global visitors tour the Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion | Image by Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority

body.x: Alongside pavilion operations, the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority carried out programs focused on global networking and creating tangible cooperation outcomes. On the evening of January 7, the “Incheon Night at CES 2026” program facilitated partnership discussions and networking among participating Incheon companies, overseas companies, and stakeholders. On January 8, the authority ran an intensive business day for visiting delegations, conducting one-on-one business meetings, and on-site business matching with buyers and investors.

Yoo Jeong-bok said, “CES 2026 serves as an important stage to present to the world Incheon’s vision of leaping from a future growth city that has led Korea’s transformation and innovation for more than 20 years into an AI City,” and added, “We will continue to do our utmost to ensure that Incheon establishes itself as a leading global AI city.”
Information on participating companies at CES 2026 and programs at the Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion is available on the official website.

Meanwhile, the Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority established the INCHEON–IFEZ Pavilion in the North Hall at CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies that evolve beyond smart city concepts into the AI era on the global stage. In addition to 10 companies participating in the INCHEON–IFEZ Pavilion, the authority linked various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, to support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards across multiple categories, setting a new record for the most awards to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness of Incheon’s innovative companies and their growth potential in the global market.
